suite_notes: THIS SUITE SCORES TOOL SELECTION, NOT ANSWERS. Each fixture asserts which tools reach the caller's top-k for an utterance; nothing here says what a correct answer contains. The answer half of the analytics gate — the verbatim questions the chat-path gate asks and the ground truth that scores them — is ../analytics-gate/QUESTIONS.json paired with ../analytics-gate/ground-truth/EXPECTED.md. The two corpora deliberately share the qNN numbering of analytics-capability-plan.md §6 and are NOT interchangeable: fixtures here carry an actor with permission_codes and expected.tool_ids, some utterances differ from the asked question (q09 states its window in QUESTIONS.json and does not here, because a window does not change which tool is selected), and this file also holds control fixtures that are not analytics questions at all — q13-admin-user-account-active is an identity question pinning the #1588 admin fast path. Reading a qNN here as the gate question is a known misreading; it cost a round of window-semantics design in #1661 and is why #1671 versioned the questions separately. Each analytics question in QUESTIONS.json names its counterpart here in tool_selection_fixture_id.

fixtures.utterance: Which customers make up most of our accounts receivable balance, and how much of each is past due?
fixtures.notes: Plan §6 Q13 — the Wave 1 full-pass gate. Answered today by AccountingFacadeTool.getAgedReceivables(asOfDate) (V39; the model does the Pareto in-context). REGRESSION LOCK for PR #1588: a live alpha smoke of this exact phrasing selected AdminFacadeTool ALONE, because the admin fast path matched the bare keyword 'accounts' and returns AdminFacadeTool as the sole candidate, suppressing every other tool. The lock is the POSITIVE assertion — AccountingFacadeTool must appear in the top-5. Under the pre-#1588 selector it cannot, because the fast path returns exactly one tool and it is not this one. Deliberately NOT a forbidden_tool_ids assertion: the first live run (2026-08-31) showed AdminFacadeTool still reaching the top-5 by ordinary semantic rank once the actor is permitted to see it, which is correct behaviour and not the defect. This fixture previously granted security:user:view to gate AdminFacadeTool in; that made the exclusion assertion incoherent — it forbade a tool the actor was entitled to. The grant is removed. q14-ar-balance-and-dso-by-month carries the exclusion assertion instead, where it holds by construction because that actor holds no admin permission at all.

fixtures.utterance: Is this user account still active?
fixtures.notes: Counterpart to q13-ar-pareto: a genuine identity/admin question must still route to AdminFacadeTool (V37 gating: security:user:view / security:permission:view / security:audit:view). Together the two fixtures pin the #1588 fix from both sides — narrowing the admin trigger must not also break real admin routing.

fixtures.utterance: Which customers are more than 60 days past due, and what open work orders do we currently have for them?
fixtures.notes: Plan §6 Q5 — Wave 1 PARTIAL pass. Aging (AccountingFacadeTool) identifies the 60+ day customers; per-customer searchWorkorders (WorkorderFacadeTool) supplies the work orders with client-side status filtering. Full pass waits on W2 E12 (status/date/technician params on WO search). Primary (scored for hit@5 / MRR) is AccountingFacadeTool because the aging call is the entry point.

fixtures.utterance: Which customers have rising sales but also rising past-due balances over the last three months?
fixtures.notes: Plan §6 Q10 — Wave 1 PARTIAL pass: the past-due half is answerable via three historical getAgedReceivables calls; the sales-trend half needs W2 E1 (revenue-by-customer) and the answer must say so. Selection-wise only the entry tool is asserted as primary (AccountingFacadeTool); InvoiceFacadeTool is listed because the model legitimately reaches for it on the sales half even though the backing aggregate does not exist yet.

fixtures.utterance: What was our accounts receivable balance and DSO at each month-end for the last 12 months?
fixtures.notes: Plan §6 Q14 — Wave 1 PARTIAL pass: the balance trend is 12 historical getAgedReceivables calls; DSO is deferred to Wave 3. Second admin-fast-path lock: the phrase 'accounts receivable' again trips the bare 'accounts' keyword, so this fixture reproduces the #1588 hijack for a different persona. NOTE (code-vs-plan conflict): FinancialReportingServiceImpl.generateAgedReceivables uses each invoice's CURRENT balance with historical aging dates, so a back-dated asOfDate does NOT reconstruct a true point-in-time balance — the plan §3 W1.2 claim and the getAgedReceivables tool description overstate this. Selection is still correct; the arithmetic half of the gate is not. Actor deliberately holds NO admin permission: with only accounting/reporting codes gated in, AdminFacadeTool cannot be returned at all, which is what makes the forbidden assertion satisfiable. q13-ar-pareto is the fixture that grants security:user:view to reproduce the #1588 hijack conditions.
